title: Prove no constant insertion makes the valuation-1 e coefficient I
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->

## Change and mathematical scope

Over F_2, insert one matrix `R` beside the stage-0 gate `I + x E_11` in the nine diagonal gates of PR #7027. The scalar `e` is central and `e^2 = 0`. The pure product remains `product_j (I + x_j E_j)` for every such insertion.

No matrix `R` with entries in `F_2[x, y, z]` makes the coefficient of `e` equal to `I`. The obstruction is diagonal: that coefficient's `i`-th diagonal entry is `R_ii` times the corresponding diagonal entry of the pure product, and each of those pure entries is a nonunit.

The coupled31 operator `(I + e I)` times the pure product is a different equation. For this one slot it holds if and only if `R = I`. That is a witness for the operator identity. It is not a T-commuting full-call word, and it does not make the coefficient equal to `I`.

Every one of the 65,536 constant matrices supported on the stage-0 block fails both equations. This is a proof for the polynomial statement and an exhaustive finite census for the stage-supported constant matrices. It is not a truncated search and not a kappa improvement. The selected frontier stays 781451/250000000.

## Task and overlap

Base commit: `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840` (canonical CrocSwap `main`, re-fetched at session start and again before submission; it had not moved). Head: `e4ddcd2fde8c46b7e528e8806ab72d9bf7690978` on fork branch `cursor/paired-star-constant-r-0aa2`.

Task card: `joint-query-controller`, scope refined. The card asks whether a changed query demand removes real work. The actual question is the first open question of PR #7027.

Overlap was refreshed at 2026-11-10T10:05:04Z with `python3 scripts/find_overlap.py`. The question is open in PR #7027 and in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5593#discussioncomment-19514176. The handoff pointer is https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19514178. No open PR solves the insertion. The unsplit two-map word, the other-idempotent census, and the g=13 and g=31 gaps were not taken. PR #6956 was not rerun.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library only.

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/paired-star-constant-r-insertion
```

Both the ordinary run and the `-O` run print `PASS_PAIRED_STAR_CONSTANT_R_INSERTION`, then `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` with outcome `negative-result`. Checks raise `SystemExit`, so optimized mode does not drop them. The direct command is `python3 -B research/paired-star-constant-r-insertion/verify.py`.

Checked counts: local coefficient `I_4` has 0 hits among 65,536 constant matrices, on either side of `E_11`; the local pure target `(1 + x) I_4` has exactly one hit, `R = I_4`; the stage-supported embedding has 0 hits for coefficient `I_8` and 0 hits for the pure product, on either side. All 64 matrix units were multiplied directly. No Lean, Docker, native, or selected-frontier replay was run.

## Credit

The paired-star contract, the operator `T`, and the pure target are from PR #5747 (Ali Romman), including PR #5673, PR #5631, and PR #5617. The T-commuting projector obstruction is PR #6956, `research/paired-star-three-full-calls`. The valuation-1 triple and the question answered here are PR #7027, head `1ba2ac5adfe58fbe9dba34d50d4e5d30633ce3d0`. Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Independent human review and a proof-assistant proof are unclaimed. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

- Can two constant matrices, placed in two different gaps of this same diagonal word, make the coefficient of `e` equal to the pure product? A single gap admits only `R = I` for that equation, but two gaps add and the off-diagonal scales depend on the gap. Any finite number of constant insertions already fails to make the coefficient equal to `I`. The first step is the off-diagonal system for insertions immediately after stage-0 `E_11` and stage-0 `E_22`.
- For the non-idempotent leading factor `N` exhibited in PR #7027, does one constant matrix beside `I + x N` make the stage-0 coefficient of `e` equal to `I`, or the eight-dimensional coefficient equal to the pure product? The diagonal identity does not apply. The first step is to expand `(I + x N)(I + e R)` and multiply by the other two non-idempotent factors.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The pinned selected record, rather than the decimal still printed in `current-priorities.md`, was the right frontier constant. https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200
